recipes.name: The Whole Jar of Peanut Butter Cookies

steps.text: In a large bowl, cream butter, white sugar, and brown sugar until smooth. Add the eggs, yolks, and vanilla; mix until fluffy. Stir in peanut butter. Sift together the flour, baking soda, and salt; stir into the peanut butter mixture. Finally, stir in the peanuts. Refrigerate the dough for at least 2 hours.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a cookie sheet.

Roll dough into walnut sized balls. Place on the prepared cookie sheet and flatten slightly with a fork. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes in the preheated oven. Cookies should look dry on top. Allow to cool for a few minutes on the cookie sheet before removing to cool completely on a rack. These cookies taste great when slightly undercooked.

raw_recipe.headline: The Whole Jar of Peanut Butter Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This cookie got its name because a whole 18-ounce jar of peanut butter is used to make it. It is the creamiest, moistest cookie I have ever had, and bound to be a favorite with anyone who makes them. Just don't over bake them!
raw_recipe.name: The Whole Jar of Peanut Butter Cookies

review.reviewBody: Oh, wow. These are soooo good! I was having a hard time trying to figure out how much was in a whole jar of Peanut butter, because I only wanted to make 1/2 recipe. In case you need to know, it's 2 cups, or 1 cup for 1/2 recipe!

YUMMY cookies!!! I followed the recipe exactly, however I used 1/2 cup shortening and 1/2 cup butter. For those of you who buy the extra large jars, the measurement for an 18 ounce jar of peanut butter is "1 7/8" cups (just measure two cups and subtract 2 tablespoons). I just use the entire two cups instead. The recipe is "forgiving" with regards to the quantity of peanut butter...give or take a few tablespoons (in my book, more is better)and they always come out delicious!!! DO NOT OVERBAKE! DO NOT WAIT FOR THE EDGES TO BROWN!! Take them out once they no longer look wet and leave on cookie sheet for at least ten minutes. TY Kevin for the recipe!!!!

I love this recipe and have used it for years. It is a very soft dough. If your dough is crumbly you probably scooped your four with out stirring it first so it is not packed. that will increase your flour by close to half a cup. I always use a wisk and stir my flour before filling my cup. Or using 1 stick of butter instead of 2 to make a cup. I just use 3 eggs I do not separate the yolk on the third egg. I usually make bar cookies out of these instead of individual cookies it really speeds it up. Once mixed I spread the dough in a full sheet pan or 2 9 X13 pans and bake 15 to 20 minutes at 350 degrees then cut into 2 inch squares while warm.. They are also great with a bag of your choice chocolate chips.

These cookies are delicious, they were a hit! They are really lovely in appearance, a wonderful texture in the mouth and perfectly peanut buttery. Super delicious cookies.
I am not a big fan of peanuts so they were omitted from the recipe. Also, I remember having these as a child and they had a light layer of sugar on the outside, giving the cookies a delightful sandy finish that is both tasty and pretty. 
In the first batch to go into the oven, one tray of dough balls got rolled in sugar before the signature fork lines were made. The other tray went in as suggested in the recipe. They both came out beautifully but the sugar rolled cookies were preferred by all. They were both spectacular, but the sugar gave the cookies a little something extra.
These were great and I will definitely make them again.

I fell in love with this recipe over two years ago and have yet to leave a review! Following the recipe I get the most amazing cookies! Also these cookies freeze very well! I double the recipe and use one jar peanut butter and one jar crunchy peanut butter!! This alone makes them so yummy but I also sometimes throw in chocolate chips to the last of the dough! That's A crowd pleaser. I get so many cookies out of a double batch I get to share! My grandkids sell them at yard sales and have repeat customers! I make mine large and refrigerating the dough at least A hour helps to keep A thick cookie

These turned out great! I didn’t have time to let the dough sit, so I didn’t do that part (which could be why the dough was so soft) so to make them a touch sweeter and more of a firm dough, I added 3/4 cup powdered sugar. My family loved them as did all my neighbors. They were gone within 10 minutes of coming out of the oven and it made over 36 cookies for me! Also I scooped them with a drop cookie scoop. This is my new go to recipe for peanut butter cookies.

BEST peanut butter cookies ever ate (after alterations).

I used a tad over 2 cups (since didn't level off top of the measuring cup w/ my knife).

I only keep self-rising on hand (so I never have to worry about adding the baking soda & salt). I only used 1.75 cups of flour leveling off the top of each measuring cup w/ my knife.

I put about 1.5 cups of the whole peanuts in a zip-lock bag & used a rolling pin to "chop"/break them up into small pieces. Ended up being a little over 1 cup of chopped peanuts, but hubby loves nuts, so I just threw the extra in (for a total of about 1.25 cups chopped nuts).

I sprinkle a tiny bit of white sugar on the tops of each cookie before putting them in the oven.

I baked these on a dark metal cookie sheet & found 350 degrees at 12 minutes to be a little TOO done (edges were turning brown which = overdone peanut butter cookie). Second batch went in for 11 minutes only & they were perfect.

We love iced cookies, so I made a simple icing (butter + powdered sugar), microwaved it a few seconds so it was runny & drizzled it over the warm cookies. So good I cried.

NOTE: 
This is also a good batter to roll into a log and deep freeze. Then you can just cut out single cookies a few at a time to make fresh cookies anytime you want. (Frozen cookies need only 10 minutes to cook as long as you cut them thin enough, 11 if you cut them a little thicker. Trial & error needed here for cook time depending on how thick you want your cookies to be.)

Read the reviews and heeded the suggestion to add ½ cup more each of peanut butter and flour and 1 tsp. of vanilla. Didn’t have butter so used shortening. Cooked them at 350 for 15. They were light, fluffy and moist. Making them again for sure!

I am always looking for the perfect cookie recipe... This one is pretty close. The one thing that is a little hard to deal with is the texture of the dough. It's a little softer than some cookies so it's a little harder to roll out. If you take it right out of the frigerator and work fast. After rolling it into a ball, then dip it into your choice of sugar, I take the fork and dip it into the sugar as well before pressing the criss-cross into it. It also helps to put the dough back into the frig between baking to stiffen back up. After they bake for 15 minutes and cooling, the cookies have a crisp on the outside and soft in the middle texture, and the flavor is great!

This is the peanut butter cookie recipe for us from now on. It make a dense, chewy, almost peanut butter fudgey cookie that is divine. The only changes I made were for convenience sake: I used a jar of crunchy, all natural peanut butter - the kind you mix yourself, and omitted adding the chopped peanuts, and I always bake on parchment, so I omitted greasing the cookie sheets. The dough keeps well in the fridge for days - haven't tried freezing it yet but I will. I now double the recipe because they go so quickly. Definitely chill for a minimum of two hours. I try to chill the dough overnight for greatest ease in handling. It's hard to keep everyone's hands out of the batter bowl, though!

The BEST peanut butter cookies I have ever made. Baked for only 12 minutes and they stayed nice and chewy. Added chocolate chips to some and they were great too. I actually doubled the recipe and rolled up three long logs in wax paper, then put the logs in plastic bags, and froze them so we could bake the cookies fresh when we're in the mood. I'm sure they won't last long though.
I make these all the time and they are wonderful with no subs. I like to freeze uncooked cookie balls and cook a few at a time so we don't eat a whole batch!
no changes

I live outside the US, and not all ingredients are easily available, and I make quite a few ajustments. BUT I try to keep proportions of fats, liquids and dry ingredients the same. I used coconut oil instead of shortning and margarine, half the sugar, added in some wheat germ to make them a bit healthier, and my special touch, after scoring the top add a bit of cinnamon sugar to the cookie. They are delicious, very delicate when hot but a bit more firm when cooled, and always a big hit. I know there are those who think any changes mean you are inventing your own recipe, but it isn't true. Thank you for helping me use a whole jar of peanut butter and making a bunch of people happy.

These are the greatest peanut butter cookies Ive ever had. I found this recipe looking for a subway cookie copy cat recipe. All or the self proclaimed copycats fell short. This is the one (: i omit the chopped nuts bc i dont prefer nuts in my cookies. Its one of those recipes you cant wait to share with people. Everytime i make them, i send the recipe to someone to beg them to try it themselves because it is THAT good. And i adore that it is such a large batch because you WILL want more. I frreze them into 10 cookie increments with different parchment paper packages and pull one out after dinner each day. It lasts us a good week or two if we do it that way. If you make them all at once, dont expect them to last! Theyre absolutely addicting.
Perfect cookie recipe to make for the family or even for a cookie exchange; just add some M & M’s on the top of each cookie before baking.
My kids love these

Best peanut butter cookies I've had. Left out the peanuts, but it didn’t matter. They were a great hit! Somewhere between a chewy and a shortbread cookie. They tasted especially good after refrigerating them. Perfect for a cup of tea, glass of milk, or just dessert!
Dissappointing. Cookies had a cake-like texture that is not traditional for peanut butter cookies. Even slack-baked cookies did not meet expectations. Flavor was fine.

I have been making these since I was a young mama and I am about to be 68!! the only thing I might do to them on occasion is sprinkle with sanding sugar or chocolate sprinkles but usually just as the recipe says.
